subject: having difficulty getting mixture model to fail

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: having difficulty getting mixture model to fail
parts:
As discussed on page 90 of BDA3 (also in earlier editions), flat-prior Bayesian inference for normal mixture models will fail because of the unbounded likelihood that you'll get when you set one of the mean parameters to exactly equal one of the data points, and then set the corresponding variance parameter to 0. Because of this, it's necessary to bound the variances away from 0 to stop this from blowing up.

So I thought I'd demonstrate this with an example. R code and the relevant Stan programs are attached.

mixture_1.stan: The normal mixture model as in the current Stan manual. It won't work because the separate modes are not identified.
mixture_2.stan: The normal mixture model using the "ordered" vector data type so that the separate modes are identified.
mixture_3.stan: Same as mixture_2.stan but switching from a weakly informative half-Cauchy prior on the sigmas (which does not exclude zero) to a weakly informative lognormal prior (which does exclude 0);

Here's what I thought would happen:
1. mixture_1.stan would fail because it would not identify the separate modes.
2. mixture_2.stan would probably work just fine but it might get stuck if any of the sigma's happened to get stuck near 0 while one of the mu's was near one of the data points.
3. We could make mixture_2.stan fail by giving it inits where the likelihood blows up. But this problem would not occur using mixture_3.stan.

Here's what actually happened:
1. mixture_1.stan indeed failed as expected.
2. mixture_2.stan with default random inits worked just fine.
3. It was almost impossible to get mixture_2.stan to blow up. By setting an extremely low value for sigma, I could do it. But then mixture_3.stan blew up too, which suggests it was just a really bad init, period, and not really the fault of the likelihood.

I'm surprised that I couldn't easily get mixture_2.stan to blow up. I guess these zones where the likelihood blows up are so narrow that Stan just tends to jump out of them in the warmup phase?

Anyway, the whole thing leaves me kind of uncomfortable. On one hand, mixture_2.stan works fine so I shouldn't complain, but I don't like using a model where the posterior blows up, even if the blow-up is in areas that are so small that Stan doesn't get stuck there.

A

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] having difficulty getting mixture model to fail
parts:
mixture_2 will blow up with MLE, but the neighborhood around zero
has vanishing volume so the posterior mass could very well be small
enough that the entire posterior still looks reasonable. You can work
this out analytically, no? In that case you could explicitly look at the
marginal posterior densities and see how much mass is around zero.
